record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.context_brief: Analytic existence far from spherical symmetry
record.original_question: Can analytic methods prove the existence of stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov solutions that are far from spherical symmetry, meaning solutions whose spatial density and net angular momentum are not merely small perturbations of known spherical or low-angular-momentum solutions, including solutions that contain ergoregions?

evidence.quote: These analytic results rely on a perturbation argument with the consequence that the constructed solutions can only be guaranteed to deviate slightly from spherically symmetric solutions and to have small total angular momentum.

Hence solutions which are far-from spherically-symmetric in the sense of spatial density and net angular momentum –in particular, solutions containing ergoregions– are not covered by these results. Accordingly, there is extensive room for analytic progress on the existence of stationary solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Vlasov system on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$: a collisionless ensemble of particles is described by a non-negative distribution function $f$ on the mass shell $\{(x,p)\in TM : g_x(p,p)=-m^2,\ p\ 	ext{future-directed}\}$ satisfying the Vlasov equation $p^\mu\partial_{x^\mu}f-\Gamma^\mu_{\alpha eta}p^\alpha p^ eta\partial_{p^\mu}f=0$, coupled to Einstein's equations $R_{\mu
u}-	frac12 R\,g_{\mu
u}=8\pi T_{\mu
u}$ with energy-momentum tensor $T_{\mu
u}(x)=\int f(x,p)\,p_\mu p_
u\, rac{dp^1 dp^2 dp^3}{|p_0|}$.

A solution is called stationary and axially symmetric if $g$ admits two commuting Killing vector fields $\xi$ (timelike at infinity) and $\eta$ (with closed orbits), and $f$ is invariant under their flows; equivalently, $f$ may be written as a function of the conserved energy $E=-g(p,\xi)$ and angular momentum $L_z=g(p,\eta)$. The spacetime contains an ergoregion if the set where $g(\xi,\xi)>0$ is non-empty. The spatial energy density is $ho(x)=T_{\mu
u}\xi^\mu n^
u$ for an appropriate normal $n$, and the total angular momentum is $J=\int T_{\mu
u}\eta^\mu n^
u\,dV$.

Existing analytic constructions, based on the implicit function theorem, produce stationary axially symmetric solutions only as small perturbations of spherically symmetric ones, with small total angular momentum $J$ and no ergoregion.

Problem: Provide an analytic (non-perturbative) existence proof of stationary axially symmetric solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov system that are far from spherical symmetry in the sense that neither the spatial density $ho$ nor the total angular momentum $J$ is required to be a small perturbation of those of a known spherical or low-angular-momentum solution. In particular, establish analytically the existence of such stationary axially symmetric solutions that contain an ergoregion.
artifact.status_search_result: Sources discussing the present status of stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov solutions describe this as an open problem: known analytic existence results rely on perturbation from spherical symmetry and yield solutions with small angular momentum and no ergoregion, while numerical solutions far from spherical symmetry (including ones with ergoregions) lack analytic existence proofs.

status_evidence.title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems include establishing methods for proving existence of axisymmetric stationary solutions which are far from spherically symmetric.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of analytically constructed stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov solutions far from spherical symmetry is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Axially Symmetric Static Solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov System
status_evidence.snippet: Analytic axially symmetric solutions obtained via the implicit function theorem are perturbations of spherically symmetric ones.
status_evidence.claim: Available analytic existence results yield only near-spherical solutions, leaving the far-from-spherical case open.
